utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case Number IT-98-29-T, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see that the copies made by the Registry, since the parties could not compromise on who would make the copies, are now distributed. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, that is D92 as you intended it to tender with the shining-through text on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We decided already that we would admit them into evidence. This is D92. We also received copies of some correspondence. After we've read them we will see what we have to do with them. Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. Still with regard to the witness who will be appearing and in particular with regard to one of these witnesses, the problems of disclosure of documents. The Defence and the Prosecution have not managed to solve this problem during the break of the weekend and of Friday, that is to say. There are two different kinds of problems in question; for one of these witnesses we received documents which apparently are of no interest to the hearing and the second witness, but this is now becoming almost a leitmotif. We are still talking about the quality of these documents which handicaps, in a very serious manner, the Defence. There is another point I would like to raise, Mr. President, and the Defence would like to file an oral motion. This will only take a few minutes. I don't know if you can authorise me to do so now. It might take a few seconds. This is the matter: For some time we have been awaiting certain responses from the Prosecution. A number of questions were put to the Prosecution and among them was a question relating to how and why certain documents which appear to be very serious, at least from the point of view from the Prosecution, with regard to Markale in particular, were perhaps doctored, manipulated. I am talking about the traces that we saw on the copies. When I say "manipulations," it means manual interventions on the document and nothing else. We haven't received any responses and I think it would be good if your Trial Chamber could fix a time limit for the Prosecution in order to finally give us a clear response as to how these modifications took place, these modifications, these manipulations in the literal sense of the term, how this came about. That is the first question that we would like to solve. So if your Trial Chamber could give an order for a time limit for this to be solved. The second question, which is just as important, Mr. President, is that we would like to know from when exactly the Prosecution knew that the shells -- we are talking about Markale, these shells which relate to the proceedings, and in the form of photographs, we have photographic records of this in any case, and naturally, within the context of the different depositions given by witnesses, we would like to know from what date the Prosecution knew that these documents were not available. Mr. President, I am asking this question about the Defence's strategy in order to enable us to prepare and in order to enable us to prepare on the basic elements that we know and if for certain reasons we cannot produce these documents, then we would like to know that this is the case. If this is not solved, then the Defence would consider that its rights have been gravely infringed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, whether there are any documents at this moment have got nothing to do with the testimony that we can expect from a witness. I think we come to that when these documents will be tendered. About the quality, I think it is also a matter of once they are going to be tendered or to be produced, then we will see what the quality is and whether the quality is acceptable for the Chamber. The manipulations, what exactly -- the manipulated documents, which ones were you exactly referring to, Mr. Piletta-Zanin?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I was referring to the documents that your Trial Chamber didn't accept, the ones on which the dates were apparently effaced. That was a manipulation, it seems, on the certificates, these autopsies, or rather, the summaries of autopsies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And then we have the third part of this about -- you are talking about a shrapnel which disappeared --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, are you able to answer to these questions now or within what period of time because the Defence asks for a response on short notice?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, it is indeed short. But I think most of these questions had been raised and the Prosecution had made certain representations and submissions. Perhaps we could have some time to consider everything that has been said today and whatever is convenient to the Court, if we could respond to these two questions, or three questions within a reasonable time. I am afraid that I am not quite certain what the second question is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The second question is an explanation on how these documents on which -- well, what Mr. Piletta-Zanin calls manipulations, have been made at least the dates. There seem to be several dates visible; one that one time had been stricken out and others that finally appear legible in the documents. They would like to have an explanation as to how this could happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: As was indicated to the Court, the evidence which we will call to explain a variety of things in this case including the -- what we would eventually submit as corrections made on documents depends to somewhat extent on the issues raised and the conduct of cross-examination. The Defence has raised the issue, the Court has indicated that it requires an explanation. We did indicate to the Court on that day that since the matter is now an issue and since the question of these post-mortem reports, or the dates on them, has been raised, we provide evidence as to how those corrections were made. I don't know if I need to give a further explanation, if I need to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You say the explanation would come once we produce the evidence in relation to these documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, it will come. The persons who can explain all of these documents are on the witness list. We -- one of them will be 92 bis. We will exercise the discretion to call that person to explain to the Court to give the evidence about how these documents were made. When I ask about the nature of the second question, I was really asking about the question in respect to the Markale incident. I am not sure if I understood what my friend is asking in respect of the Markale incident

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think this is the medical -- at least, the death -- the medical records indicating the cause of death of the witnesses. I think that is what Mr. Piletta-Zanin calls the manipulated documents and they were related to the Markale incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I thought my friend asked --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The third one was the shrapnel issue, whether there was an explanation why the pieces of shrapnel which are photographed, we have seen the photographs, why they are still missing. We had some explanation on to that, something about a removal of office, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If that is the question. I think the question is a little bit unclear and my friend does not think that what the Court suggests is the question is the question --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, with all due respect, that is not quite the question. The question related to knowing - and the Prosecution could tell me this at the end of the hearing - the question was from what date the Prosecution knew that these determining elements, these pieces of shrapnel, from what date they knew that these pieces of shrapnel could not be traced whereas, there were photographic records and in the testimony given by various witnesses, this was also referred to. The witnesses called by the Prosecution referred to it. The question is simply: From what date did the Prosecution know that it could no longer produce this shrapnel? This is an important question for the Defence because we have based our defence also on the idea that these documents would be produced, whereas we see that this is not the case. So if we have to lose a considerable amount of time to prepare a strategy in order to produce documents to contact people, physicists, chemists, et cetera, on the basis of the documents that we were told we would get but which we have not received, in that case, the Defence will draw certain logical conclusions from this. That is what we are interested in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question is on from what moment the Prosecution who provided photographs of shrapnel pieces, on from what date the Prosecution knew that they could not -- well, that these pieces were not available any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I will try to obtain the precise date and convey that information to my learned friend through the Court or to him directly, as he suggests.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could this be done by tomorrow? Is that a fair time limit?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: By tomorrow we will do all that is necessary to have that information available.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. Stamp. I think then we reach the moment where the Prosecution could call its next witness and that would be, if I am well informed, Mr. Enver Taslaman.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Indeed it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Usher, could you please bring the witness into the courtroom. Good afternoon. Mr. Taslaman, I presume. From your answer, I take it you can hear me in a language you understand.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Taslaman, before giving your testimony in this court, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a solemn declaration that you will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth. The text of this declaration will be given to you now by the usher and may I invite you to make that declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please be seated. Mr. Taslaman, you will first be examined by counsel for the Prosecution. Mr. Stamp, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Stamp:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir. Could you please tell the Court your name.

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: My name is Enver Taslaman, I was born on the 23rd of February, 1933, in Skopje, the former Republic of Macedonia, and I lived in Sarajevo and Mostar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you work presently, Mr. Taslaman?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: I am retired.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now you said you lived in Sarajevo. Where do you live now?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: I still live in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you live there between the period of 1990 and 1995?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: In 1991, we were expelled from that settlement and as a refugee I lived in another part which is called the C5 settlement or the C5 area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you live in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: Sarajevo, yes. Naturally in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what is the district that you refer to as C5 normally called, or where exactly is it?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: That area is in the place where these shells fell, where these pumps were located.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: C5, as you refer to it, is in which part of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: Yes. Dobrinja. Dobrinja.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it the area sometimes referred to as the airport settlement?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: I lived in the airport settlement and we were expelled in 1991. And as refugee, we moved to live in the C5 area and that is part of Dobrinja.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in 1993 during the conflict that occurred in Sarajevo, were you in any way employed as a result of that conflict?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: No, I was a pensioner. I have been a pensioner since 1978.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in respect to that conflict, did you in any way participate in community activities in 1993?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you, I was a disabled pensioner. I was not able to participate in any kinds of conflict and I am too old to be active. All I could do was work for the civilian protection.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in 1993, were you assigned any particular task in respect to your work for the civilian protection?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: Well, when humanitarian aid would arrive, it would be distributed. We helped and then we went on duty. We made sure that people could obtain water and pump water and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were your responsibilities in respect to pumping water or obtaining water in 1993?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: When I was on duty for the water, there was a pump there and only two could go there at a time. One would pump the water and the other one would collect it. When the bucket would be filled, another person would come to pump and the person who was pumping before, he would take water.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You seem to be speaking about a particular time or a particular situation. I am asking you generally, what generally were your responsibilities during 1993 or the earlier part of 1993 in respect to the distribution of water in the community that you lived in?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: I was a guard for the water. I had to let people pump the water, that was my task. I had to prevent all of them from entering the yard at the same time. I only allowed two of them to enter at a time. One person would pump and the other person would fill up his bucket.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in the early part of 1993, did you or may I -- withdraw that. Why did people in your community have to get water from a pump in the yard, in a yard?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: Well, our water is very good and there are good sources in Bosnia, but our enemies cut the water supply off. We were forced to -- well, luckily, these private houses had this water. They also had a normal water supply which would come from the sources, but when the supply was cut off, their supply was cut off too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very slight problem of translation. If we can't use the term "aggression," in this Tribunal, then this term should not be used. "Aggressor" should not be used. In the French transcript, I think that I noticed this. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see in the English transcript the word "enemies." What is the part where the witness stated about cutting off the water?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, it was this word "enemies" that I heard, and I think that I heard it translated in the French transcript, Mr. President, as "aggressor." And for the reasons that we know, I wanted to draw your attention, I wanted to draw the attention to the booth to this fact.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The word "aggressor," this is why we interpreted as "agresseur."

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Should I answer?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. I am just asking you, Mr. Taslaman -- we usually speak about the other party or you indicate what the party is. And we usually refrain from qualifications as to "aggressors," or if you could do so, and of course if there is a specific reason why we use these words, you can use them but if you are just referring to the other party, we prefer to say it in a rather neutral term since this Court does not know at this moment whether there was aggression, who was an aggressor. We still have to hear the whole case before we could interpret these words properly. So if you could do that, unless there is a specific reason why you would choose other language, but then please then indicate why you use it. Mr. Stamp, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I take it from your answer that water sometimes ran in the pipes in the homes of the community where you lived; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: Of course. Because it was the 20th century and we lived in a big city as Sarajevo and we had powerful forces of water and then we were put into a situation in which we had to go out and collect water and carry 30 litres of water --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Taslaman. Please listen to what I ask and answer it. We will take it step by step. Sometimes the water which ran in the pipes to your homes was cut off; that is correct?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: For the most part it was cut off since the start of the hostilities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that is the reason why people went to pumps for water; is that what you were expressing earlier?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, can you recall the 12th of July, 1993?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: [No translation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear the question that I am asking you? Can you remember the 12th of July, 1993?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: I didn't hear what you said.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: There is probably no translation.

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: I will try and remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 12th of July, 1993, at about midday of that day, were you on duty anywhere in respect of your work for the civil protection group?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: That is correct. On the 12th of July, around 1500 hours, that shell landed, and it was an enemy shell, if we can call them like that, and then a massacre happened on that particular day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before we get to the shell falling, Mr. Taslaman, I would be grateful if you would just listen to what I ask and answer, just respond to the questions. What were you doing there that day? That is what I am asking you. Were you on duty there with respect to your duties with the civil protection?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: On that particular day, I was on duty and I was there, allowing people to collect water and then when any two people left, the other two were allowed to come and collect water.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where exactly -- where exactly in your community were you on duty?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: I was on duty at the pump in the yard of Mujezinovic, where the pump was working that day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you remember the name of the street?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: The name of the street was changed several times. First of all, it was called Brane Buljica Aleja, then it was called Cane Babovica, and then after the liberation, or after the end of the war or whatever you want to call it, it was Babovica; it was changed again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember what it was called in 1993?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: I think the name was Babovica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, how were the people organised to collect this water?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: To get water, well, people would put it in to plastic canisters or buckets or oil canisters, 30 litres each. They were allowed to pour 30 litres each.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now you said you allowed two people at a time to go to the pump. Where exactly was the pump in the yard?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: About four or five metres away from the gates.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you said "the gates," would this be the front gate?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: The gate which marked the entry into the yard, into the courtyard of the building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how were the people organised before they were let into the yard?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: When any one person left, the other one went in because it was their turn to collect water. And the person who had remained in pumped it. Because we necessarily had to have two people in there at any given time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At about 15.00 hours, about how many people were in the vicinity waiting to collect water?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: Well, I can't really tell you exactly, but there were people on both sides of the building and they moved close to their canisters, simply to move them forward because it was about 150 metres away from where they had put their canisters and buckets.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. Can you give us an estimate of approximately how many people were waiting for water at about 3.00 on the 12th of July, 1993?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: Well, since the pump across the street was out of order, perhaps anything between 100 and 150 people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if two were let into the yard at the pump at one time, where were the other people wait?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: They were waiting along the sides of the buildings, near the staircases and the door.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Piletta-Zanin with all due respect, the French booth is telling me that the Prosecution is extremely difficult to hear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, the French booth has some difficulties in hearing you. Please speak as loud as possible, not as possible, but loud enough to be understood.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: There is a small problem with my microphone. Sometimes it virtually explodes in my ear. That's why I turned it down at one stage. But it seems to be fine now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Problem solved.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, apparently there is a problem with the channel in the French booth because they said the accused replies instead of the Prosecution replies, so I just wanted to clarify that point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I didn't hear the accused speak.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I am informed that part of the problem might be caused in the B/C/S English booth where, while not translating, the microphone is still open, as far as I understand, and I am informed that it would help us if the microphone would be put off. I don't know whether it is true or not, but that's just my information. Could you please see whether you can help in solving the problem. Mr. Stamp, let's try again and see whether we can continue in such a way that everyone hears whatever he needs to hear.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said the other people would be outside waiting along the sides of building and near the staircases. Would that be on the road outside the yard where the pump was?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: Alongside the buildings. Because first you've got those private houses, and then there was a district called Hakije Turajlica to the left, and to the right there is the Babovica side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am talking about the people who were outside. They would be lined up along the street?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: Alongside buildings and on the staircases. They were not standing outside in the street except for when they had to move their canisters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the weather like that afternoon?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, it was fair and sunny, but afterwards, when I was wounded myself, it started to rain, and when that shell --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am afraid I don't follow your answer. It was fair and sunny at what time of that day?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: It was fair, sunny. Do you understand now?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. It was fair and sunny. At what time of the day you said it started to rain? In other words, when was it fair and sunny and about when did it begin to rain?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: It started to rain at around 5.00. I had already gone to the hospital by then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. Now there was a conflict going on in Sarajevo at the time. Do you know where the confrontation lines were or how far the confrontation lines were from this water pump?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: The demarcation line went through the airport settlement. As the crow flies, it is about 150 to 200 metres, more or less.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the composition of the crowd that were waiting to collect water that day? Were they old people or young people; let's start with that, generally speaking.

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: Sixty per cent elderly. Then some people maybe more than 20 perhaps, some more than 18. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were there soldiers amongst the crowd that day, waiting for water?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: Rarely. They had their own pump down by the demarcation line. Perhaps a soldier might have come along. One can't follow all the developments.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any there that day?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: Maybe one, but I can't be sure. Because for the most part, it was where the civilians used to come because there was a queue and you had to wait and waste more time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. You said that the soldiers had their own pump down by the demarcation line. About how far was the soldiers' pump from the pump that you were gathered at?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: It was about 250 metres to the right because it was down there, where they had the lines. It was at a private house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, approximately how many women or what proportion of the crowd was made up of women waiting for water that day at your pump that you guarded?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: I didn't quite hear the question. Could you repeat it, please. How many women or --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. What proportion of the crowd was women?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: What proportion? Well, it depended. We had men and women. I can't tell exactly how many women there were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you said a shell fell at about 3.00 in the afternoon; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you when the shell fell?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: I always used to sit in the courtyard where the pump was because the gate was about two metres away from where I was sitting. So when one person was about to leave, I would let another one in, in order to have them help the other person who had pumped the water earlier collect the water for themselves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So I take it that at the time when the shell fell, you were sitting in the courtyard; is that your answer?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the shell fell, what did you see or hear, if anything?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: Well, first of all, I felt something because I was wounded in my right arm and in my left thigh. And another man was wounded in the courtyard and I saw him and then I moved towards the gate and then I saw the massacre. And then the cars came along and I was taken by that first car, and another young boy whose insides were coming out, and we were taken to the hospital.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's take it step by step. You were sitting in the courtyard when the shell came. Did you hear anything immediately before the shell exploded?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: The shell landed on somebody's hand, a woman's hand, so the explosion was not quite as far -- as loud as it would have been had it hit the asphalt, but the shrapnel was everywhere.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear the shell as it approached?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: No. No, I didn't hear anything at all because the pump was in operation. People were pumping water and we couldn't have heard any noise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said when you went to the gate, you saw a massacre. Describe what you mean. Tell us exactly what you saw.

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: I saw corpses down by the canisters and then shrapnel everywhere, dead bodies on both sides. I came out to get First Aid and then a couple of cars came along - a Golf Volkswagen and other cars with inhabitants living there - and they took us to the hospital.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which hospital did you go to?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: Dobrinja, the Dobrinja hospital.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you treated there?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: Yes. I was operated on by a Dr. Hadzir, who was the head of that hospital. And others were treated by Dr. Cravic and the others.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you discharged that day or were you admitted?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: No. Three days later when other wounded people came along and then I was taken to the hospital to have my wounds treated afterwards on a daily basis because the capacity of the hospital was not all that great.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: With your leave, Mr. President, Your Honours, I wish to show to the witness a medical certificate which is marked P1517A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Leave is granted.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have a --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. One of the problems that we have had with this document once again has to do with our difficulties in reading it. Some parts apparently have not been translated and especially it seems to me that the name of the person here is not the same as the name of the witness here. Quite simply, I don't know what's happened, whether the Prosecution can clarify this in any way. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, if you would take it that the document relates to another person than this witness because the name is not the same, you are perfectly entitled to ask the witness during cross-examination on whether it was him -- well, whatever questions you would like to put to him. So that would not be a reason, but the other two things you said is the illegibility of the copy and the parts not translated.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, in other words, Mr. Chairman, if we look at the copy that we have received, and we have already complained about it in the past, it seems to me that once again there are overlaps to the right side of this paper where you can see something which is completely illegible on the top of the page. I think there is something coming from a mechanic stamp above the word "Skopje" and then you can see that there are some lines of the text which are transparent, Mr. Chairman. You can see a couple of dots but you don't really know what these dots stand for. We don't know if this is a certified copy of the original, but we can't really tell what it is about. The same applies to the left-hand side where you can see that there are a couple of lines. Apparently there was some text there. All we can see here in our copy are dots and apparently this has not been translated either. The same applies, apparently, to what is meant to be below and above this "IM Ratka 13" which is not legible before, either what is above or below that line is not legible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you inspect the copy of the file of the Prosecution, Mr. Piletta-Zanin?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Chairman, we could indeed ask the Prosecution if they could provide us with a better copy, but the thing is, that we have always asked for the originals as well in order to see clear, and in order to make it possible to the Defence to organise the defence in a logical manner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. But I think the Chamber instructed both parties that if they would receive illegible documents or partly illegible documents that the first thing they should do is to address the other party and even fill in the form we provided you with. Mr. Stamp, it has been asked of you to have a better legible copy or was there any specific complaint about P1517A?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: This is the first time I am hearing about a complaint.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed for the time being, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Taslaman, do you see a name on the document near the top left of the document?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: I think it's clear and perfectly legible. The name and the family name, everything, my occupation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The name that you see there, is it, you said, your name. But is it spelled correctly?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: Taslaman is the way it should be and not Teslamen. My father is Saleh, my name is and I was born in 1933 and I am a pensioner. If it is unclear to anyone, I have a mark -- I have traces of the wounds on my body and I would be happy to show them. And this refers to myself. This document refers to myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Chairman, I would just like to clarify this. I do apologise in advance. As a matter of fact we have received this form from you, that is correct, but on the same day we had already submitted a request and it was communicated, it was a confidential one, it was D3441 and it included that particular page. It is dated the 10th of April and it included this page and here the copy is even less clear than the one we've got today and we had already complained about it at the time. Ever since, we have received nothing from the Prosecution, either explanations or a better copy of the document which that -- which has to be said, must be said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, the complaint is that the document provided to the Defence was even less legible as the one you are producing now and this is a document on which certain parts -- looks as if there is a stamp in the right upper-hand corner -- is not clearly legible either. Do you have any better copies of this document or could you, as you did sometimes, show what is the copy as it appears in your own file?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: We brought our best copy to Court. He can inspect it if he is inclined to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, perhaps we -- so that is the best copy you can produce?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: This is our original here

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, can you please first show it to Mr. Piletta-Zanin and then to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I just want to say this: I have examined the documents that the Prosecution has provided us with and I notice that it is one of these documents that we term "sensitive." It has to do with a reception of a document which was faxed in general, the kind -- this is the kind of paper that one uses for this. I am saying this because there is obviously an original that was faxed and it is quite sure that this original was faxed and that this original is much clearer than the document that was received. And this is why we are demanding the original, as always, and demanding that the Prosecution finally provides documents that are totally clear, which is to say, the originals. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, the Chamber has the power to ask for authentication of documents. Is this document part of the evidence you intend to submit to the Chamber as far as the medical documents are concerned? We know that there is a request for admission into evidence of some testimony related to medical documents where in written statements witnesses give their -- give information about -- is this part of it or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: May I just confer?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: It is not intended to be brought in through the 92 bis statements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Mr. Stamp, for your information. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, we will give the decision on the admissibility. Of course, you are entitled to cross-examine the witness on the document. I think that is the first step to be taken. May I at least make the follow observation: That there is no absolute right of either party to receive originals of documents. Of course, it is a different matter when the originals can be obtained, whether the parties should do their utmost best to produce these originals but there is no absolute right as such to have only original documents admitted into evidence. May I just return the documents. Yes. Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. The Defence is quite aware of the fact that there are limitations, that its rights are limited. But what we would like to say is that, in spite of the examination of this document, which is, in inverted commas, the best the document which we have available now, we have noticed that the number of protocol is not on this document. I think that the Prosecution could at least indicate the number of the protocol so that, if necessary, the Defence can carry out all the necessary research. Because these documents don't have this information, at least we should be provided with this information in oral manner. Thank you in advance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What do you exactly mean by the number of the protocol? The hospital protocol or --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. President. We saw when we were receiving other testimonies that, in each medical record for certain hospitals, we saw that each document had a protocol number, that is to say, what the number of the record, the medical record was, and the number of the patient was; but these documents, we don't have them and I would like this to be submitted to us and to you. And if the Defence is to carry out its work, this technical information is absolutely essential to it for us to verify it and to carry out our cross-examination. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You do not -- I see one number which seems not to relate to a date or which is just a four-digit number. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, is this --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, concerning the document that we received, since it is very -- it is not very legible, I can see two dates; 1.846 and another 1.836, I think perhaps, or 1.946, perhaps. Are you talking about one of these numbers?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. As a matter of fact, in order to even make the confusion greater, I would rather read it as 1346, but that is the number I was referring to, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As there is nothing on the document, we don't know whether this is what is in question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So you are asked an oral answer from the Prosecution. Mr. Stamp, whenever you are able to give that answer, would you please then do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps during the next break you could make some efforts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, where were you born?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: I was born in Skopje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... the next document.

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: Yes, in the right margin, and in 1933, that is the date of birth. This is certainly the record. 1.946.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ultimately the Court will have to decide whether or not it is a record, Mr. Taslaman. Could you just answer my question for the time being. Were you a pensioner on the 12th of June, 1993?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: Since 1978 I have been a pensioner since that year as I said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see pensioner written here on this document?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: Yes on the left-hand side, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said your father's name is Saleh. Do you see Saleh written here in this document?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I can see it, in brackets.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see the words I.M. Ratka 13, on this document?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: That is Ivice Marujica Ratka 13, yes. That is a street, the name of a street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In respect, can you tell us anything about that street that you mentioned, where were you living?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: I was in two locations: Ivice Marujica Ratka number 13 and later in Vase Butozana 1. I changed two flats.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You said you were treated by Dr. Hadzir. Do you see Dr. Hadzir at the bottom of this document?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it here at the front and on this other one. His name is printed: It says Dr. Hadzir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You said that you could show us where -- well don't show us. Just tell us exactly where you were injured.

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: That is evidence that will confirm this

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President I apologise for intervening again I think there is an error in the transcript I see that part of my name has been mentioned in line 15. I don't know if this is a habit perhaps or something that the witness may actually have said. We could ask the witness to say this again clearly to have him say what the name of the street in which he lived is. I don't know if this was an error in the transcript or not. Can you see that? It is page 26, line 15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see it, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, but as you know, the evening hours, the tapes are better listened, especially in respect of names so that can be put properly in the English translation. I did not hear anything about your name and yes, I think proper care will be taken that what the witness said will be correctly in the transcript. I think it is more or less a, how do you say this, it is more or less a -- it is not a detail, but it is what you hear sometimes on paper. It looks -- it may have sound almost -- phonetic, yes, that is the word I was trying to find. Thank you very much for your assistance

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is a pleasure, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I was asking about where you got injured by the fragments that day.

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: Here in my arm, on my arm. If necessary, I can show my left leg. It is very clear evidence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Earlier you had said left thigh.

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: Please, I am quite ready.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No you don't have to show us. Which --

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: The left thigh, in my right arm. I can show you the wounds to my arm. If necessary, I can show it to the booth. That is this wound.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I don't know if the Court saw, but the witness did indicate his left buttock area. I don't think there is any necessity for him to show us unless my friend requires it in evidence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that there were many people injured and some dead. Can you remember who some of these people were?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: Yes. Well I know that Dragica died. She is someone I knew personally. And then Ibrahim Talic and his wife.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's take them one by one. Do you know Dragica -- do you know her full name?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: No, I don't. I was a refugee in that area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where she was when the mortar exploded?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: She was nearby. I think she was supposed to be the second person to enter and then a shell fell. Part of her brain fell on me. I was in the vicinity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said Ibrahim Talic and his wife?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: Ibrahim Talic, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you speak to him that day before the incident?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: With Ibrahim Talic? Are you referring to him?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: Yes, I did. Every day he would go to collect water with his wife and he would then return home to rest. I told him, "Ibrahim, go home, have a rest. Rest while your wife is waiting." He said, "Why you telling me to go? I don't go." And that was his fate. His fate was to die there with her.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know any of the other people who were injured or killed there? You spoken of Dragica.

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: Yes, the Mujezinovic family. I know the man. He lost his wife and two daughters. He will come to testify here tomorrow, too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, I just ask whether the witness just mentioned names of protected witnesses. I have a few on my list for the next coming days.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then it must be in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The name that he mentioned, although it is perhaps not idealist to put it on the transcript, is not the name of a protected witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the 12th of July, 1993, did the pump continue in operation?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: Well, it did because we would dig wells. I didn't dig them but people in Dobrinja V did. Then in the yards and schoolyards they would dig wells in places where there were gym halls and then the line diminished here because there was another pump in operation, one at Duda Mujezinovic, so the line diminished.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said a well was dug in a schoolyard. Can you say when this well was dug?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: Yes. That was after the massacre, after that massacre of ours. I think it was half a year later. I can't remember exactly. That was a gym in the school that had been devastated and people broke through the blackboards, through the surface, and they got to the drinking water.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you say what happened to that well that was dug at the gym?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: Well, people would go and collect drinking water there and a shell fell there and five people were killed too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The people who went to collect drinking water there, including the five that were killed there, were they people who fought, that is combatants, or were they civilians?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: They were civilians, civilians, only civilians. But it was closer. They didn't want to go further down because that was quite far away, about 800 metres from the school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you explain what you mean when you said that they didn't want to go further down because that is quite far away, could you clarify that, please?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: Well, there was a series of buildings such as its place where the school was and where a well had been dug. It was in front of their doors, that was Dobrinja II B or II A, and they would use water here. Whereas we were about 800 metres away, that is, where we went to collect water and where I was on guard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The well where five people were killed at, can you recall when this occurred, when the shelling occurred?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: I can't remember the date because I was passing through there. I was working as the collaborator for the television. I would collect television subscriptions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it before or after the events in which you were injured on the 12th of July, 1993?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: It was after.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you say about how long after?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: I think it was about half a year after that because that is when they worked on it, maybe six months later. I can't say exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Approximately six months later is your answer. Do you recall in September 19 -- I beg your pardon -- in September 2001 participating in a filming of the site at which the events that you speak of today occurred?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in that film, did you show an OTP investigator certain places relevant to this incident?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I think there is a video recording where they were filming --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise for interrupting, but the transcript in French must be verified because we didn't ask whether an investigation was carried out into certain locations relevant to this investigation, but only whether the witness showed the investigator certain places. I think this is of crucial importance, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think proper care will be taken of your observation, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, for the final version of the transcript. Please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President. With your leave, Mr. President, Your Honours, could the witness be shown, Exhibit P32

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, we will have a break in approximately five minutes. Will you be able to do your questioning on the videotape as well, because otherwise it might not be fresh in the memory of the witness of what he saw. So if you could do it in four or five minutes. If not, perhaps if there is any other subjects you would like to touch, perhaps do it now and play the videotape after the break so it is fresh in the memory of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I don't know if it would be convenient to the Court to take the break now, then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: A bit early and then not to start any new subject. Yes. Mr. Taslaman, if you would play a video now and have a break, you might have forgotten about it already after the break. So, we will have a break a bit earlier than usual and the video will then be played after the break. We will have a break until a quarter past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: --- Upon resuming at 4.17 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, you may proceed to examine the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I am grateful, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Taslaman, the pump in question which was shelled the 12th of July, 1993, do you know when --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think we had some technical interruption but I think it is over. Please proceed, Mr. Stamp. They started already playing the video. That is a bit earlier than we expected.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I think I will get to the video in due course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know when that pump had been installed?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: Those are houses which before the settlement were built had already been there and they had those pumps before they had any other urban water supply. Because the settlement I lived in was built in 1978, 24 years, that is, and there is other houses where at least -- well, more than 30 years old.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The pump that we are speaking about where the shell fell near to in July, 1993, can you say for what purpose it had been installed?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: Because there was no urban water supply and they used to get water from that pump before they had water in the house. And also afterwards they used it for watering the garden.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had this pump been installed before the war?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: It had existed. All that existed before, and then it was being used. For example, I don't know, somebody had their own courtyard and they would use the water from the well to water the plants rather than paying for the water which came from the city waterworks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would the existence of the pump be known generally within the community before the war and during the war?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: Yes, it was known before the war and that is why it was targeted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there another pump close to where the pump that was shelled?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: Across the street perhaps 8 to 10 metres away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was that pump operational on the 12th of July, 1993?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: No, it wasn't. Because the well was being cleaned. There was mud inside. At Duda Mujezinovic they were cleaning the well and so the only pump in operation was the other one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, prior to the time at approximately 15.00 hours when the shell fell on the 12th of July, 1993, had any other shells fallen in that area that day, on that particular day?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: Let me tell you. The shelling could happen at any time. We were basically there for them on a platter, the snipers could shoot at any time. But that shell landed on that particular day and caused the massacre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, what I want to ask you, that day up until that shell had any other shells fallen in the area or was that the first shell that fell in the area that day, that particular day?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: On that day, the first one landed in that area where the water was being pumped on that particular day. Otherwise, there was shelling day and night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I take it from your answer that the first one which landed was the shell which caused what you referred to as a massacre?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You spoke about sniping which you said was something which happened frequently in that community. Could you tell us about it. From where did the sniping come?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: That sniper fire, for the most part, came from the Hidrone settlement, from the orthodox church. Since Dobrinja, on the way down to us, is rather low, they could shoot, the snipers could shoot, for example, from Dobrinja, from Kaledza Street [phoen] and also from Milanka Pupavica Street [phoen]. From those streets.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you say which party to the conflict, whether it was a Bosnian Serb army or the army of Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina which controlled those areas from which the sniping came?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: It was from the Republika Srpska. It was under their control.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in the vicinity of this water pump which was shelled on the 12th of July, 1993, were there any military facilities that you know of?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: No. It was an exclusively civilian area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before the break, you were telling us about a video presentation that you participated in. I would like you now, with the leave of the Court, to have a look at a video, which may be played.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: May I?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. It is P3281C. Can the video be played, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: "THE INVESTIGATOR ON TAPE: I am not asking you to speak, but could you please show me to the best of your recollection where the pump was at this location on the 12th of July, 1993. "THE WITNESS: [Indicates] "THE INVESTIGATOR ON TAPE: Can you now please show me where to the best of your recollection you were standing at the time the shell exploded on the 12th of July, 1993. "THE WITNESS: [Indicates] "THE INVESTIGATOR ON TAPE: Can you now please show me by standing in the location where to the best of your recollection a line of people started on the street on the 12th of July, 1993. "THE WITNESS: [Indicates] "THE INVESTIGATOR ON TAPE: Mr. Taslaman, can you now indicate by pointing with your arm in which direction to the best of your recollection the line of people extended on the 12th of July, 1993. "THE WITNESS: [Indicates] "THE INVESTIGATOR ON TAPE: For the camera, could you please point again. "THE WITNESS: [Indicates] "THE INVESTIGATOR ON TAPE: Thank you. Could you please now show me where to the best of your recollection the other water pump was located in this area. "THE WITNESS: [Indicates] "THE INVESTIGATOR ON TAPE: Thank you."

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The last place you indicated in that video was a house where there was another water pump located and you have told us earlier that this house was across the street. Can you say who owned that house with that other pump?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: Mrs. Mujezinovic, Duda.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you say whether or not she or anybody using that other pump was injured by the shelling or sniping that occurred during the conflict?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: She was wounded by incendiary bullets afterwards and she spent about a fortnight at a hospital. Her skin was burned while she was pumping water for herself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Firstly, when that shell exploded, were you sitting or standing inside the yard, can you recall? I ask you that because I think you said in answer to me that you were sitting, and on the video I think you were asked to show where you were standing. Can you recall whether you were sitting or standing?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: I was there, as you saw on the video. I showed you where I was standing and I had my back turned to the doors of the grand floor. Sometimes I was crouching on the floor because I didn't have any chance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you went outside after the shell exploded, can you say about where the bodies of the deceased and injured people were?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: When I came out where people who had the cars had driven to take people to the hospital, and I myself was taken to the hospital, in the vicinity of those buildings and perhaps on both sides of the building. I don't really know because I was taken to the hospital immediately with that young guy whose entrails were spilling out. Who had also been wounded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Taslaman

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: That, if it please you, Mr. President, is the end of the examination in chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stamp. Is the defence ready to cross-examine the witness? Mr. Taslaman, you will now be examined by counsel for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. With your leave, I would like to cross-examine the witness. Cross-examined by Mr. Piletta-Zanin:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, sir. Sir, you mentioned you worked for the Civil Defence; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you have mentioned about you had worked for the Civil Defence within the framework of Dobrinja; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: That's correct, Dobrinja. But it was called Objekt C5, settlement C5, that was the name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, have you in your capacity as somebody who was cooperating with the Civil Defence, have you had any contacts with any other members from any other sections of the Civil Defence?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: There was pensioners and we worked for between three to four hours and then another shift came along and then we were allowed to go home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, that wasn't my question. My question was about whether you had any contacts with other people, other officials from other sections, other parts of the Civil Defence? For example, whether in Alipasino Polje there was somebody in charge of the Civil Defence and, in that case, did you have any contact between the officials from Alipasino Polje and the officials in C5?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: Well, Alipasino Polje had no contact with us because we had our own Civil Defence in C5. And our boss was Mevluda Mujezinovic who was the head of the Civil Defence for us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Thank you, Mr. Witness. I would just like to submit a map to you and I would mention a couple of points. But to begin with, could you tell us whether you know where the headquarters of the Civil Defence was, both for Dobrinja and for C5?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: You mean you want me to show it on the map? It is not clear. Or do I have to say that --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well the question, sir, is whether you know where the headquarters are and then I'll show you the map.

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: The headquarters was in the street of Luja Pastera that was the headquarters of the Civil Defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The headquarters of the Civil Defence for Dobrinja in general and for C5?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: And the headquarters was in Dobrinja but the one I mentioned before was for C5, for the suburb or settlement for C5 and the headquarters was in Dobrinja.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I am going to ask the usher if the president allows me to submit to you a map.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [In English] That is for the witness and this is a black and white copy for the other parties. [Interpretation] Mr. President, we have simply made black and white photocopies for everybody else and there is a coloured copy for the witness for the practical reasons that you are familiar with, but of course it is one and the same map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness do you see on the screen to your right a map, a geographical map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Taslaman, the original is to your right. Perhaps you could...

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, quite simply, do you recognise this as being a map of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: Yes, of course. This is the commune of Novi Grad and the Lijo [phoen] to the left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, I am going to stop you here. Now we can see, I believe, the area which is of interest, that is to say, the airport area, do you recognise this area?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: Yes I do know the streets C4 of the airport Chapika [phoen] Dorica [phoen], Belmanova [phoen], Fransa Preshevna [phoen].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, since you have recognised the map, could you now please show on the map and indicate by number 1 the headquarters of the Civil Defence that you said you were familiar with? No, no, no, write. I would like to ask you once you recognised it to write this number and you have to check that it is the right colour. Could you recognise the place that we are talking about on this map?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. As a consequence, could you now take a pen, please. The usher will give it to you and could you mark on this map just place number 1 on that spot.

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, could you please write number 1 next to this mark that you have made.

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: [Marks]. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right then. We will proceed differently later on. Thank you very much. Would you now, Mr. Witness, mark the second centre of command by marking a cross there, because otherwise we won't see it. Put a cross on this map for the second headquarters that you have mentioned. Just place a cross there, please.

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: Yes, I put a circle there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could we have a finer pen, please

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...with a black marker which is a bit thinner.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is very good, Witness. Thank you very much. Now, on this map, could you find, are you able to find the location of the headquarters of the 5th Motorised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: No, I can't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, Witness, could you indicate on this map the place where the incident of the 12th of July, 1993, took place.

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: There is no street --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do please take the pointer to show it to us. To your right. To your right. To your right, Witness.

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: This looks more like Dobrinja II.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is on the right side.

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: No, I don't see the street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, it may well be that the name of the street is not indicated, but do you recognise the area?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: I don't see the street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have understood --

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: It would be somewhere around here. This is the street of Luja Pastera, the main headquarters C5.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you please take this fine-tipped pen and mark by a triangle the place where the incident took place.

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: It would be somewhere around here because I don't see the street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do please mark that.

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, could you now please show us, on the basis of your memory, where the front line was in this part of town, in other words, within or close to C5?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: It divided the street Akva Seremeta in C4. On the one side were the Republika Srpska people and on the other side were our armed forces and they were simply divided by a road. That was where the front lines were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, could you indicate or trace that front line on the map that you have to your right.

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: This was the dividing road, Akva Seremeta. It went through the entire area but I can only see a part of that, a section of that road here, but it went all the way down to the main road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, could you please draw that line, that front line, the section of that front line that went through the settlement that we are interested in. Could you take the pen and draw that front line on the map.

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: Do I put a cross in there?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, you have to draw the entire line, the separation line, the demarcation line.

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: Yes, it went like this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you continue. Did the line stop there?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: Yes. I don't see clear on this map. I assumed a small section of the street Akva Seremeta.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you certain, Witness, that there are no other front lines as far as you know, no other demarcation lines?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, could you wait, please. Could you wait for me to finish my questions. You have said that, as far as you knew, the front lines separating the parties were at about 250 metres, as the crow flies, away from the incident; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, which is the front line that you are referring to, the one you drew here?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: Yes, this one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, and you are absolutely certain that there are no other front lines, that there were no other front lines at the time on the 12th of July, 1993 in the vicinity of this spot?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: There were no other front lines, just this one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir. In your capacity as an expert for the Civil Defence, were you informed of the existence of nuclear shelters around or near Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: In Dobrinja III there was shelter, but over in our area, there was nothing, just in Dobrinja III.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you show us, sir, where in your opinion those nuclear shelters were situated? Wait a minute. Perhaps you could circle the area so that we can find our way through this area where the nuclear shelters were situated, if you can.

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: It is somewhere around here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, could you please draw a circle around this area so that we can find it later on in the transcript. Draw a circle.

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. So it is a circle which is close to 400 or 406, I can't read it very well on the screen. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Witness, are there any other areas where there were nuclear shelters?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Both numbers appear on the map. I would clarify that it is near to 406.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I always said that the Bench could see better than I can, and this has now been confirmed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, were there any other locations apart from the one you have just indicated?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: I don't know of any other ones.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you know whether these shelters were used by the army?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: No, they weren't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say, "no," I see the transcript says -- I can see the entire response to this question in the transcript. Thank you. Witness, I want to return to -- we can forget the map for the moment, but it can stay on the ELMO. I have a series of different questions but we will return to the map later on. Witness, do you know whether at a certain point in time in this conflict the two sides, the Serbian and the so-called Muslim side, do you know whether these two sides reached an agreement with regard to the issue of water?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
