utterances.text: As far as I know, there was no agreement between the two sides. But later on, as Dayton approached, they started -- water started arriving again. That is what happened. I wasn't aware of an agreement nor were other citizens in the area where we lived.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether during the period, the so-called war, do you know whether there were any interventions or any discussions with representatives of UNPROFOR and with sides in the conflict with the objective of obtaining an agreement with regard to the issue of water?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: We didn't have any electricity so we were not able to follow these agreements because we were without electricity. So I didn't know anything about the agreements that they tried to reach.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you don't know anything about this?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, can you confirm whether at the beginning of July, at the very beginning of July, 1993, and during the three weeks following that date, do you know whether there were any important -- whether there were any large-scale conflicts in the Sarajevo area as part of the taking of Mount Igman? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: I don't know because I wasn't in the battlefield so I wasn't able to know and I said that the news we got was very meager, we didn't get much news because we didn't have any electricity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, did you live at that time in Sarajevo? I think I heard you say that you did.

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: Yes, I lived in Sarajevo. But, for example, in the battlefield there were barricades there and the citizens could not reach these areas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I am not asking you whether you lived in Vojnicko Polje or elsewhere, what I am asking you is whether you lived there. Your answer was yes. Did you live in the south part of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: I lived in Novi Grad municipality, in the Dobrinja area, in the C5 part, the C5 sector.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Is it true to say that this area was an area which faced Mount Igman?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: The area in which I lived, there were buildings in a series in the Cane Babovic Street and I wasn't able to see Igman from there. My flat was located in such a place that I was not able to see Igman. I could only see Dobrinja

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, may I please make a pause and may I ask you as well, Mr. Taslaman, to just have a short break before answering the question because Mr. Piletta-Zanin can understand your language and you can -- if the interpreters need some time to translate what Mr. Piletta-Zanin says. So if you would look at your screen, as soon as the text stops moving, then the interpreters have translated what has been said and you see now it is moving presumably and when I stop talking, then it continues moving for a while and then it stops. So would you please wait until then before answering the question. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I shall bear with the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I didn't ask you where your flat was, but I asked you whether the area in which you live faced in the direction of Mount Igman. This is a question which one can answer by saying yes or no.

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have a map on your right. Let's have a look at the map again. Could you show us on this map where Mount Igman is located with regard to Dobrinja? Could you please do this, without marking it, please.

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: Well, Igman is in fact across the road of the airport, east of the airport tarmac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the other side of the tarmac, does that mean to the south of the tarmac?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, would you agree with me that after the Dobrinja area and the airport in general, we could say that Mount Igman is situated after these locations?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, since you lived there at that time, did you hear the sound of heavy fighting in the period from the 1st of July and during the following weeks, did you hear heavy fighting in order to take Mount Igman?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: No, I didn't hear anything. At that time I had a wife that was ill and a child who was seriously ill and I was spending more time with my family. I wasn't spending -- paying attention to these battlefields.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you said that you didn't have electricity and that the media was not functioning; is that correct? Could you confirm that, please?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the media wasn't functioning and since this was the case you were not able to get any news; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, if the media was not functioning for you, then the case would be the same for your neighbours; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: No. If they had special electricity supplied, well I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you, Witness. I would like to continue -- I would like to continue with two or three other questions. Witness, a minute ago you said that you had seen the person who had unfortunately been hit by this shell. Can you confirm this? I am talking about the incident of the 12th of July, 1993; yes or no? Could you please answer the question?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness you said that this shell hit an arm. Can you confirm this?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And was this a woman's arm, can you confirm this too, please?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, her surname was Simic or something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, you spoke about, just a minute ago when responding to one of the Prosecution's question, you said that it was a shell that had been fired by the adversary. Witness, are you a ballistics expert?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, have you ever fired shells yourself?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: I have been retired since 1978.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That wasn't my question. Sorry to interrupt you. I am asking you whether in the course of your life you have ever fired a shell: Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what a ballistic ellipsis is?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what the margin of error is when firing -- very well. Witness, how can you know since you are not an expert? How can you know that this shell came from the adversary's camp? How can you know this for certain?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: Well, there was a commissioner that investigated this later. I am not an expert in these matters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. So you are telling us that this was the result of someone else's opinion; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you know whether an order was issued by the authorities, by the municipal authorities, I think, to avoid the grouping of a number of persons?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: People would not gather in one position. They would enter the buildings, the stairways and this is where they could go. Then when the canisters were brought, the plastic containers, then they would approach too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But do you know whether there was an official instruction to the effect that too many people should not gather together in certain places in the town?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: In the town of Sarajevo, no, I didn't have the opportunity of hearing this because I didn't have any electricity in the place where I was living.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Can you tell us when this committee that you mentioned assembled and when it presented the conclusions it had arrived at?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: After the incident that took place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, Witness. I hope that it wasn't before the incident. But my question was related to the date; was it six months later, was it immediately after the incident, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: After the incident. As soon as I went to the hospital, the police then came and the investigation was carried out immediately. They are not going to carry out an investigation six months late.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you yourself questioned by this committee?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know why?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: I was in hospital.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you had been discharged from the hospital, and I think you were there for only three days.

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: The committee didn't come to see me but these people from the international did. I was in the Ministry of the Interior at first.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did this take place? Could you be precise?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: Well, there was traffic. It was possible to go into town at that time and these international representatives had turned up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you be more precise? Could you give us some dates or tell us about the approximate duration after the incident?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: Well, you have the statements there which I have signed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't know what you have signed but I am asking you a question, Witness. I would simply like to know whether, as far as you can remember today, I would clearly like to know whether you remember what you have spoken about, what you indicated.

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: What I said so far, yes, I remember all of that. But when I gave the statement, no, I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. So then is it right to consider that you don't remember this clearly today; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: I don't remember the date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, I am referring to the dates. Very well, thank you, Witness. I would like to -- thank you for the booths. I would like to return to something else that you mentioned in your statement. Could you please formulate that answer.

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: About the well, I know when they were digging it. That was in the gym in the school and people would collect water there so as not to have to go very far. It was nearer for them there and there was a massacre there; a shell fell and five people were killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will interrupt you then, excuse me, but can you tell me what the name of that school was?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: I can't remember the name because that school had a different name. Now the name is different again. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you don't remember the former name?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, do you know whether it was a technical school or a high school or a school for young children?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: It was a primary school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. And was the school functioning as an institution at the time? And I am referring to July 1993.

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, do you know whether this school and I am referring to the premises of the school, do you know whether they were used for other objectives, other than to give lessens?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: No, it was not possible to use it because we didn't have any fuel for heating. We had no means of cooking food.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, I am not talking about lessons.

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: Nothing was used. That was a deserted building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, could you please, as we are talking about a deserted school, could you please indicate on the map where the school was located? Would this be possible? I can show you -- I think that we need the assistance of the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please assist, Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: It should be here between the Dobrinja Hospital, somewhere here. That is where the school was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Witness, could you indicate it by marking it with the letter E? Could you mark it with the letter E?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: Well it's very small. Very small and there is no street to help one find one's bearings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Thank you, Witness, for your help. Witness, given that you worked for the Civil Defence, do you know whether the army gave orders to the Civil Defence?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "no," does that mean that you didn't know or that the army didn't give any orders?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: No, the army had nothing to do with the Civil Defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Civil Defence, did it participate in the elaboration of the second line of defence from a distance or from a proximity?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: The Civil Defence distributed humanitarian aid and assigned people to go on duty where the water was being distributed. These were people who were fairly old, over 65 years of age, 66 and on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, who helped the army in digging the trenches, do you know anything about this?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you know whether civilians were engaged to participate in the digging of trenches?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: They were younger people for sure. I didn't participate in this and I didn't have such a role in the local commune. My role was --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I have to interrupt you. Do you know whether civilians participated in digging the trenches; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: Perhaps younger people, but no one of my age. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. But I am not talking about people of your age. Did you see any civilians who were participating in this war effort, that is to say, were digging trenches?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: Perhaps the main Civil Defence, but I didn't have any contact with them because no trenches were dug in the place where I lived.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. So, Witness, would it be correct -- I apologise. Excuse me. Witness, would you agree with me that the Civil Defence in general could have participated in this defence task, in general terms?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: Maybe, but I didn't know anything about that because I wasn't part of that formation. As I said, I was on duty at the pump --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, thank you. Witness, I am going to present to you -- just a minute, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, Witness, do you know what the military formation was, which military formation supervised the sectors that we are talking about, that is to say, Dobrinja E, C5, do you know what military formation supervised this?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: No, I don't know which formations did that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Usher, I am going to ask for your assistance to present this document. I think there is a sufficient number of copies for everyone. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I do not read the language which we find on this document. I see that there is no translation but if it would be --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [In English] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- but you are asking about details of the subject just touched upon. Could you perhaps please take the earphones from the witness, from his head. This seems to be a military document but we have now consistently heard the answer of the witness that he had no contact, he didn't know what part of the army was responsible for that area. I hope, and I certainly would regret if you would continue asking him about things he testified again and again that he didn't know anything about. And I will -- I think that would be useless, but of course I can't read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, you will be given a response but this is from the 5th Motorised Brigade, this is where the document comes from. The question I am interested in, I would like the witness to read a few lines below and have this -- these lines translated into English to show that it comes from a military document. It will be translated and, on the basis of that, I will ask another question. So we are talking about the second line of the three lines that we have here below. This is what interests me in particular. I won't mention the name here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is a subject of which the witness just testified that he doesn't know anything about?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The difficulty I would raise --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, there is difficulties in reading. As you know, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, we especially in relation with the context, especially of these short documents, we ask the Defence to provide with a translation. So therefore we will perhaps just first put your questions to the witness, but then give us perhaps, if you are able to do so, to give us a -- first of all, a general, I would say, summary of what the document is about and I can't imagine that Mr. Stamp would not even be happy to have just a summary but he would like to have a translation. We discussed this before. I don't know what efforts you took to get a translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, we still don't have a translation in the form desired by Mr. Stamp. But here it is just a matter of establishing the dates and the formations of the various units that are of interest to the Defence. One is with regard to the second line. Mr. President, I can't mention the name for a very simple reason that you are all familiar with, but as soon as I get the translation, I will let Mr. Stamp have it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... ask the witness on whether he knows anything about the subject covered by these documents because --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- then we don't have continue with the document. You have not answered my question what efforts you made in order to get the document translated. You confirmed that there was no translation, but what efforts you took to have it translated, I have heard no answer yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I didn't deal with that particular problem, Mr. President. I can talk it over with my colleague and I will give you a reply shortly. I don't really know, but we will look into it in a moment, if you authorise us to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you just pick up your headphones? Thank you, Witness. Witness, you have in front of you the document that is going to be submitted to you. Can you see it? Witness?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Quite simply, is this is a document which formally comes from the command of the 5th Motorised Brigade, on the basis of what you can see written on the document, of course? Witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... can the witness identify the document? Does he know anything about the document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that is the first question you have to ask him. If you provide us with a translation, we can all read what it says, whether it is of the 5th Motorised Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right, then, I will proceed differently.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, on the basis of the principle that this document comes from the command of the 5th Motorised Brigade, would you please read the line -- could you please read the line starting by a date which is the date of the 22nd of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I instructed you to first ask the witness in general whether he knows anything about what the subject perhaps that this particular -- so first let's ask whether he has any knowledge of what you would like to tell him about

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, quite. That is what I was going to do by asking the witness to read the first line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you know anything about what is mentioned in this document, that is to say, the period of time where a number of units or entities were set up such as the Territorial Defence in Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: No, I am not familiar with it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You do not know when it was set up in Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, as a consequence it doesn't make sense for me to have the witness read this document and we won't submit it in relation to this witness, because the Witness is not familiar and does not know about the setting up of the Territorial Defence in Dobrinja. Witness, do you know where the police headquarters was in Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: Well, I have come here as a witness to a specific massacre and you are asking me questions which have nothing to do with it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Taslaman, you have been called as a witness by the Prosecution because the Prosecution expects you to tell us about the massacre. Since you are here the Defence might be interested to hear from you whatever knowledge you may have which might be of importance for the Defence and which might not directly relate to the questions that have been put to you by the Prosecution. The Defence is entitled to do so, so if you know anything about what the Defence asks you, tell us so that the Chamber also will hear your answers. Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, could you reply to this question: Did you know where the police headquarters was at the time?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: I did not, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, do you know whether at the time when these events took place, do you know whether the armed forces had or did not have equipment and uniforms?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: They did have uniforms, nothing else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, I'd like to continue with other questions. Could you show on this map -- no. First of all, I withdraw this question. I will rephrase it. Do you know where was the entry into the tunnel which to a certain extent went beneath the airport -- below the runways of the airport and coming out on the other side of the airport? Did you know where the entry into the tunnel was?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: Well, after the massacre, the digging of the tunnel started five or six months after that. Well it did exist. I can't tell you any lies because that is where the foreign representatives went through and everybody and that tunnel saved Dobrinja by bringing food through the tunnel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, since you are referring to food I am going to talk about restaurants. Do you know of the restaurant Sunsis [phoen]?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have never heard of a Sunsis [phoen] Restaurant in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if there is a shopping centre where there could have been a restaurant similar to the name of Sunsis [phoen]?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: You mean in Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Quite.

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: There was no shopping centre in Dobrinja.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether in that shopping centre there was a special penitentiary unit, a special prison?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "no," you said that you did not know or that it wasn't there, a special prison?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, I am going to show you a couple of pictures. Could we look at P1386, it is a set of photos which have already been submitted for another dossier. But before we do that, I am going to try to ask another question of the witness to gain time. What is, generally speaking, the colour of the licence plates in Sarajevo? Is it white?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: Yes, white. White, and then the letters of the alphabet. We no longer have licence plates indicated the place names, Sarajevo, Banja Luka what-have-you. Just the alphabet.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Madam, there this set for you here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, the Registrar is still trying to find it. It is not just a matter of having the copy but also the matter of relating it to other witnesses. We don't know exactly when it was tendered and admitted into evidence. If there is another subject that you could deal with and in the meanwhile, Madam Registrar will find it for us.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I will be pleased to do so whilst waiting. And at any rate, if we need it, the document is there, for the time being, I will continue with my cross-examination of the witness. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, since you were in the Civil Defence, do you know where the barracks, the soldiers' barracks were situated?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: There were no barracks there, as far as I know, because those were residential buildings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, but you do know and you do agree with me that there were soldiers in this area that you were living in; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: There were people who would travel to the front line, but there are no barracks. For example, people lived with their own families but there were no barracks there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, were did these people sleep at night? I mean, okay, they spent a day at the front line and where did they spend the night, where did they sleep the next day?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: At their homes, with their families. Where else?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't know, that is the question I am putting to you. Where did they have their meals? Were there any canteens there?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: I suppose they must have had restaurants someplace but they were given food. I suppose they could get food from their families because there were no real kitchens and there were no barracks for the army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, have you yourself seen any soldiers, either one or two in groups, carrying arms, in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: Do you mean in the city of Sarajevo or in Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Both. One or the other.

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: I did not go into Sarajevo because there were barricades at Vojnicko Polje. That is something I've already said. The soldiers who were in Dobrinja did go to the front line. I don't know if they were armed, but they didn't carry arms through the settlement where I lived.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: Yes, I did say that. They didn't carry any arms. Perhaps when they went and were on duty at the front line, I suppose they had arms there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you know whether the Territorial Defence had any presence in Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We even have difficulties in finding a date when it was tendered. So perhaps if you could just show it to the Chamber. Perhaps it comes back to our memory.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unfortunately, the date was not mentioned by the Prosecution, but the actual document is 1386P.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What I see, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, is that it is indicated that 1386 is going to be -- at least, it is expected to be tendered if witness Jusuf Spajic will testify in this court. I don't know -- that is where I find it on my list and the Registry has really great difficulties in finding that it ever has been admitted into evidence. It has not.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please -- perhaps my recollection will help me. If the document is -- yes, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I do apologise, but I can hear no translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, let's first see that we can understand each other again.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I am sorry, but since I looked at P and so on and so forth, I don't have it any more, it is you who have the document now, but I worked on the assumption that it had already been tendered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This had left your --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, I'm sorry, I have it. I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please give it to the usher first so that he can give it to the Registry so that we will see whether our memory can assist us.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know whether --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is in none of the Judges' recollection that we have seen this document before.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Mr. President, we will look through the list. I am very sorry but this is a document coming from the Prosecution which bears a stamp, as you can see, and it may well be that it had not been produced. But it doesn't really matter. We can tender --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... if you want to tender it as a Defence Exhibit because you think you need it in relation to the testimony of this witness. But you would have -- well, of course, then you might have no copies prepared as well?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, since we worked on the assumption that it had already been tendered. I would just like to show these --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Bench is certainly correct. I apologise. May I have the document back, madam. Thank you very much. We are going to proceed if the Bench authorises me to do so. I will put the photos on the screen so that everybody can see them --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- and in that way we will all know what we are talking about. I would like to put 00269704 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: May I respectfully ask if before that is done, if I can have a brief look at the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, of course, you may.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You can have the copy for Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, this is not -- may I see the copies? I am not fully aware of -- do you want to indicate that this is the copies that you received?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These are the copies that we had received at the beginning. I am not sure. But it doesn't really matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, we want to pay serious attention to bad copies. We don't want you to make this courtroom your playground. We are not interested in having illegible copies. Madam Registrar, would you please have it returned to Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise, Mr. President. What I was asking for was for this document to be put on the screen, the one that the Prosecution has at the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you have inspected it? Yes. Please put it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But, Mr. President, it just so happens that the documents that we've got here are the ones that we initially received from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I told you that I will not allow you to make this courtroom your playground. I will and this Chamber, the proper -- will pay proper attention to bad copies and just as we blame the Prosecution for providing copies which have not been checked as to the legibility or as to the quality, we are not amused by reciprocal -- well almost and I don't want any further comment on it as well. I made quite clear to you that presenting bad pages to the Chamber is of no use and is not appropriate. I don't want any further comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed with the cross-examination of this witness

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have the photos now on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, could you please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, is this a picture taken as far as you can remember after the incident that we are talking about?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: I am familiar with this picture. This is around where the water was being taken, but who took the picture, I don't know, I wasn't present. Because once again as I have already said, I was hospitalized.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you confirm that this is the place, this is the place where this incident would have happened to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: Yes, approximately, that's the location.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I would like for you to be shown another series of pictures, but before we move on, let me ask you whether you can see on this photo a mineralogical plate -- a licence plate, sorry.

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: I don't see any licence plates.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see if the canisters are damaged in this photo? Can you show us where?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: I can't show you. All I can see that they are in that carriage down there in the direction of the water but I don't see where the damage is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see a single canister which is supposed to be damaged?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: If that dot -- yeah, there in the carriage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fine. Could you describe the extent of damage that you have just shown?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you, I was among the first people taken to the hospital.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, Witness, I am asking you whether you could see any water recipients which were damaged on this photo and, if so, which ones; and if you can, could you perhaps describe the way in which these recipients were damaged?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: It is not clear to me. Perhaps it was the part further up and the shell landed further down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have heard you say in your own language, "I cannot," which did not appear in the transcript. So for the purposes of the transcript, I did hear you say, "I cannot." Can you please turn the pages of this document and show us the next page, please. Witness, can you see on this picture any legible licence plates? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: I can see something, but those are the old Sarajevo licence plates. SA --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you show us on the screen where exactly you can see that, on the car. Could you read what you can see there, if you do see something?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: It is a hazy picture.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you are unable to read it, tell us.

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: I can't, it is hazy. I can't read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Usher, could you continue on to the next picture, please. The next one, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you find it easier to read it on this picture?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: I can see scattered canisters, a damaged car, I don't see what this is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next picture, please. The next one. I am sorry. Continue. The previous one, rather. Right there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, can you see the licence plates of this car?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: I don't see them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you read them?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: No, I don't see them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: I can't read something which doesn't exist. I can tell you that I can see the chairs and the table.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This concludes the cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I have already mentioned no further questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, before we have a break, could you please inform the Chamber whether there is any need to re-examine the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: There will be. Having regard to those photographs, I think we might well use the opportunity over the break to regularise that and get some more copies for the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if that would be possible, I think the Defence would be grateful if you would do so and you might have prepared them already. Mr. Taslaman, since there are some more questions to be put to you by counsel for the Prosecution and perhaps also by the Judges, I don't know yet, we will have a break until 10 minutes past 6.00 and we will adjourn until 10 past.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: --- Upon resuming at 6.14 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp. Are you ready to re-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Re-examined by Mr. Stamp:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the course of your evidence, you were asked to mark a map, Mr. Taslaman. Could you say whether or not you have any special training or experience in map reading?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: No, I haven't. I was a machinist for the railways. Nothing to do with maps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The places that you marked on the map, then, would it be correct to say that they are mere estimations of where you believe places are?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said at one time that the shell hit a lady's arm or hit some part of a lady's body. Did you actually see this or was it something that you heard of later on?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: Something that I heard later on because I was taken to hospital.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And finally, can you recall if, when you were in hospital, if you were spoken to by any member of the police service?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: I can't remember. I don't remember speaking to a member of the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If that would please you, Mr. President, Your Honours, that would be the re-examination. I was hoping that by now I would have been able to provide copies of the document that was shown so that we could have the witness have a look at everything while everyone had copies. However, we are not in a position to do so now and we will do so at a time when it is scheduled to be done. If I may just have a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, that is all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Taslaman, I have got one question for you. Could perhaps the Exhibit or the document P1517A be shown again to the witness. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Taslaman, you have answered some questions about this document. Have you ever seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: I have. I have such a document when I was discharged from the hospital. This is diagnosis that says that I had been admitted to hospital.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is this document the same as the document you received when you were discharged from the hospital?

utterances.speaker: ENVER TASLAMAN
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your answers. Mr. Taslaman, this concludes your testimony you've given in this court. I know it is a very long way to come from Sarajevo to The Hague. It is a long journey. I hope you understand that it is very important for this Chamber to hear the testimony of those who have been present during those years in Sarajevo and to hear their answers to both the questions of the Prosecution and the questions of the Defence and additional questions from the Judges because it will assist us in performing our task. So, we would like to thank you very much for having come to The Hague and I hope that you will return home safely.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, could you please lead Mr. Taslaman out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, thank you. With your permission, I would just like to deal with an issue which arose with regard to certain documents when my colleague wanted them to be shown to our colleague, Mr. Stamp. We received from our colleagues the document 1517. We have a list which we received on the 12th of April and we have the following witnesses; Pasa Menemda [phoen] and two others. We have the following documents: The Defence's interpretation, since it states 1517 since that is the number stated, we were preparing ourselves for the hearing and we took the document 1517. In this document -- and I'm saying this because I want to avoid situations of this kind in the future -- in this document there is a photograph which I asked my colleague to show to Mr. Stamp since we didn't know which document, which photo document was in question. The copy that we gave you for the witness was for you and the witness to have a look at. It was legible. So the Defence's intention was not at any time to cause an incident in the Trial Chamber. I would like, accordingly, to say which documents will be tendered into evidence out of 1517. Every document under 1517 has its own page. My colleagues could have noted and that 1517 would be admitted but that it would be a medical document. I wouldn't want you to think that the Defence had the intention of presenting documents to the Trial Chamber, documents which were not appropriate. We would just like to indicate that this document for the Defence, 1517, this is the document. This is the document I took. I thought that this was the document that my colleagues wanted to have tendered into evidence, however, I don't understand why this misunderstanding arose today and, in order to avoid future misunderstandings, I would ask my colleagues -- we'll have this document for Blagic [phoen] and Mekolic [phoen] for these witnesses. These are documents which the Defence has. They are about 30 pages and it contains photo documentation too. So I do not understand what my colleagues intend to tender as evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, as I have instructed the parties again and again is that these kinds of issues should be settled during the breaks, during the weekends, at night, but not in court. If there is any document which you can't read, ask the Prosecution first. If you say I've got a set of documents and well, I can't distinguish them because they are all black, then you ask to the Prosecution what these documents are about. You inspect the originals or you ask for better copies and as soon as you show them entirely black copies, and if they would refuse to give you any better copies, then just address the Chamber and we will see what to do with it. But we are not going to spend time in court about that. If it becomes unclear 1517 for three witnesses, which will be tendered or not, then ask them what is on these photographs so that you do know before we enter into this courtroom. That is -- I don't -- and this Chamber don't want to be confronted with problems if the parties have not first tried to solve them. Especially these kind of practical problems. Let us forget as soon as possible about black page being given to the Court for whatever reason. It should have been done out of court and if it is done in court, that is one mistake and if you do not check them before giving them to the Chamber, it is another mistake. Let's forget about it. We are not here to see whether we can exploit problems, but whether we can solve problems. If that is an answer to our observation.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Madam Registrar, could you please guide us as far as the documents are concerned.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P1517A, medical documentation B/C/S --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. I have a very serious objection to raise. In order to be able to develop this objection I should be in a position to show you very clear copies of other documents that I have so that everyone can understand why we are raising this objection here. I didn't want to mention this just a minute ago because it seems that the witness in question is a protected witness and I didn't want to cause any problems of any kind because we are not here to create problems. But what we could do on the basis of this document which I would like to show everyone and which I will not show on the screen for the moment because it contains names which -- the names of protected individuals, we could state why we are raising objection to the presentation of this document. If we should go into closed session, I don't know. This is for you to decide before I continue with this objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If the -- if show the other document is really material for your objection, I think we should turn in closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 12 Pages 7256 redacted, closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we are in open session again.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P1517A.1, English translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Also admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P3281C, video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D93, map marked by witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Also admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D94, a booklet containing photographs, B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that is also admitted into evidence. And -- yes, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence didn't want to suggest this document of photographs to be tendered as evidence since we only have the one copy. We can make copies of these photographs because, in future, we won't be able to work with other witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I take it, Mr. Stamp, that since you were preparing for admitting into evidence these photographs that -- or did you not yet finish that? But I would rather not. If the document is admitted into evidence, I would rather not break the chain of custody and give it to one of the parties.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I think -- perhaps if we could agree, we could supply the Defence with another set sometime tomorrow or this week or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: -- if the Defence does not want it to go into evidence, we do not object to them withdrawing it, because we do intend to present this document at a later date and ask that it be received in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What we could do is perhaps -- it has been tendered in evidence now. It is just a matter of who is going to provide the copies. Since the Defence has no copies any more. I am aware that the Prosecution might have better facilities to prepare copies, although there is a lot of complaints about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we don't want to tender this document into evidence. We just wanted to show it to the witness. We wanted to show this document to the witness so that he could recognise it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, what questions have you put to him in respect of these documents. It was not just showing whether he recognised it. There was quite a lot of -- and apart from that, part of the testimony of the witness becomes not well understandable if these documents are not admitted into evidence. So I think the Court needs the documents, the Chamber needs them and --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: We have copies here of the documents with translations. I don't know if we could present these to the Defence and perhaps an agreement can be arrived at. We have reproductions of the document presented by the Defence. These reproductions are not laminated, I think the expression is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If, they're clear copies, also of the photographs with the translations, then --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Perhaps the Defence could have a look at them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, could you give one copy to Mr. Piletta-Zanin? Let me do it otherwise. I would like to hear by tomorrow in which may this evidence will be tendered let's not -- I mean -- so we do not take any decision this very moment, but let's not spend more time on it in court. Mr. Usher gets tired from transporting the copies from one side of the courtroom to the other. Madam Registrar, the decision is therefore not taking yet on D93, it was? D94, I apologise. Is there no other documents, then, Mr. Stamp, is the Prosecution ready to call its next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Indeed we are, Mr. President and that is Husein Grebic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, would you please guide the witness into the courtroom. Can you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I just assume that you are Mr. Grebic. Mr. Grebic, before giving testimony of this court the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a solemn declaration that you will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth. The text of this solemn declaration will be given to you now by the usher. May I invite you to make that declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please be seated, Mr. Grebic. I already announced to you that your testimony today will not last much longer than a quarter of an hour but since we try to use our time as efficiently as possible, we nevertheless asked the Prosecution to call you at this very moment, but presumably your testimony -- your examination will continue tomorrow. You will first be examined by counsel for the Prosecution. Mr. Stamp, please proceed. Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise for raising this matter in the presence of the witness, but I have to do so. The Defence wants to say that it intervened with the Prosecution in order to ask what was the case with the documents that it wanted to submit. Because on the 10th of April they said they would be presenting a certain series of documents perhaps as evidence and then it seems on the 12th that it would present other documents. So the Defence has been running after documents. I have written to the Prosecution. We have written to them in order to obtain a clear and definitive answer and I think it would be good if we could obtain this answer. I regret having to ask these questions in the Trial Chamber. But as we have received no reply, I am obliged to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is relevant in view of the witness to be examined at this moment? Is it once again 1517?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not only 1517 but also 162, Mr. President. And these are documents which I listed in a letter of the 10th of April for the period of the 11th to the 12th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I suggest to the parties that we will now start the examination-in-chief and we have only one quarter of an hour left and then you have from 7.00 until quarter past 2.00 tomorrow to see whether you can solve the problem or not. If not, I would like to hear from you by a quarter past 2.00 or during the first break.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Stamp:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is your name Husein Grebic?

utterances.speaker: Husein Grebic
utterances.text: Yes, my name is Husein Grebic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is your occupation, Mr. Grebic?

utterances.speaker: Husein Grebic
utterances.text: I am a salesman and I work in trade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where do you live?

utterances.speaker: Husein Grebic
utterances.text: I live in Sarajevo, in the Dobrinja district.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the conflict that took place in Sarajevo in the early 1990s, where did you live?

utterances.speaker: Husein Grebic
utterances.text: In the beginning of the '90s, I used to live in Sarajevo in my own flat which was a part of Dobrinja IV, at the Gandhi Street, number 2, floor number 1, apartment number 5.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Chairman, Mr. President -- no, I withdraw.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And though you might not have lived at the same place, did you continue to live in Sarajevo during this period?

utterances.speaker: Husein Grebic
utterances.text: I lived in Dobrinja IV, district number 5, in my own flat, up until the 13th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that, did you -- did you remain in Dobrinja or did you move out of Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: Husein Grebic
utterances.text: I moved into town and I was there until the beginning of June and then I went to Dobrinja II and Milesta Street, number 7.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the course of the conflict?

utterances.speaker: Husein Grebic
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I am afraid I was getting some feedback that was quite disturbing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I must say, I don't hear your voice in my earphones. I can hear directly, but your English doesn't come to my ears by way of earphones. Perhaps it's better now. I don't know whether there's any particular problem, but let's just proceed and whoever has problems with the sound, please tell me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you join any particular organisation during the conflict?

utterances.speaker: Husein Grebic
utterances.text: I joined the armed forces of Bosnia-Herzegovina by the end of April, 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And for how long did you remain there in that organisation?

utterances.speaker: Husein Grebic
utterances.text: I stayed in the army up until the 25th of December, 1995.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What, if you could tell us in a sentence, were your duties while you were a member of the army?

utterances.speaker: Husein Grebic
utterances.text: My duties were that of a foot soldier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where were you posted when you were on duty with the army?

utterances.speaker: Husein Grebic
utterances.text: I was on the line, on the demarcation line and apart from that, I was staying in my apartment when I had time off.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Mr. President, I am quite sure the witness said something after --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters, unfortunately, did not hear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, perhaps the witness could repeat the last part of his answer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you said that you stayed in your apartment when you had time off and then you went on to say something else. Could you repeat it, please.

utterances.speaker: Husein Grebic
utterances.text: I said that when I was on duty, I was at the demarcation line, I was a guard. And when I had time off, I was in a flat where I lived during the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In July of 1993, where did you live?

utterances.speaker: Husein Grebic
utterances.text: In Sarajevo, in the district called Dobrinja.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us which part of Dobrinja you lived at?

utterances.speaker: Husein Grebic
utterances.text: I lived in Dobrinja II, Street Emila Zole 7, floor 6, apartment 28.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I would like to take you to the 12th of July, 1993. Did you go anywhere in particular that day?

utterances.speaker: Husein Grebic
utterances.text: I remember the 12th of July, 1993. There was a serious massacre at the well where people used to come and collect water. And I myself was wounded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I take it you were wounded in this serious massacre at the well?

utterances.speaker: Husein Grebic
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you -- well, why did you go there, may I put it that way?

utterances.speaker: Husein Grebic
utterances.text: I didn't go to collect water on that particular day, but since my sister was a refugee in that house where the well was, I went to visit my daughter -- my sister.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At about what time did you arrive there that day?

utterances.speaker: Husein Grebic
utterances.text: I can't quite remember what time it was. But I do know that a serious massacre happened on the 12th of July in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you arrived there at the house where your sister was temporarily a resident, did you see people around?

utterances.speaker: Husein Grebic
utterances.text: Yes, I saw quite a few people, women and children with lots of canisters, plastic canisters and buckets.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where were these people, women and children?

utterances.speaker: Husein Grebic
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were they?

utterances.speaker: Husein Grebic
utterances.text: They were standing in the street and the well was in the courtyard of the house and so there was a crowd and in order to avoid a bigger crowd, there were guards from the Civil Defence and they allowed two, perhaps three people in at a time to collect water and the others had to wait in front of the gates in the street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you pass the people who were waiting at the gate and into the yard?

utterances.speaker: Husein Grebic
utterances.text: Yes. I did pass there and I saw some people I knew by sight and some people I have been in touch with during the war and before the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you go to in the yard?

utterances.speaker: Husein Grebic
utterances.text: I entered the courtyard through the iron gates and I was standing in front of the door to the house, the front door.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And while there, did anything happen?

utterances.speaker: Husein Grebic
utterances.text: Yes, sir. Was all standing in front of the door and I was knocking on the front door because I wanted my sister to come outside so I could give her something. She didn't hear me knocking. So I knocked once, twice and three times. Meanwhile -- at that moment, I felt a burning sensation to the right of my body, the entire length of my body on the right side whereupon I felt -- I heard a strong detonation and explosion. It was a grenade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From which direction did this sound come, the explosion that you speak of?

utterances.speaker: Husein Grebic
utterances.text: I couldn't hear the sound but the explosion came from somewhere to my right. So somewhere around the gates to the courtyard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, before you heard this explosion and felt this burning, were you speaking with anyone?

utterances.speaker: Husein Grebic
utterances.text: Before entering the courtyard where the water was being collected, I met a friend, a woman I knew, she was a friend of my sister's, Mrs. Dragica. I said hello to her and we made small talk and then I went on to knock on the front door of the house where my sister was living. And then the shell landed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So after the shell landed, what did you see or hear?

utterances.speaker: Husein Grebic
utterances.text: At that particular moment, I was unable to see anything because I threw myself into the corridor of the house because I was expecting another shell to land because normally they followed one another. And as I threw myself into the corridor, into the hall, my sister and a friend of hers who was visiting, Devla, came and helped me. I stayed within the house for a quarter of an hour, maybe 20 minutes, and when I came out of the house, I saw a lot of dead bodies and a lot of bodies in pieces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said your sister and a friend of hers helped you. What, if anything, happened to you?

utterances.speaker: Husein Grebic
utterances.text: First of all, they stopped the bleeding, so as not to lose any more blood. They tried to stop the blood. And then I went out to go to the hospital.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, what happened to you? What caused the bleeding? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: Husein Grebic
utterances.text: The bleeding was caused by this shell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where were you injured, what part of your body?

utterances.speaker: Husein Grebic
utterances.text: The entire right side of my body from the foot to the shoulder.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you came out of the house eventually, did you go anywhere?

utterances.speaker: Husein Grebic
utterances.text: I was going to go to the hospital on my own. I was unable to. A young guy came long. He was called Sejo Mujezinovic and he took me to a hospital that is within Dobrinja, within the settlement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you treated there?

utterances.speaker: Husein Grebic
utterances.text: Since I was one of the last patients to get there, I had to wait for the other wounded to be treated and I was one of the last to receive treatment. I received medical treatment and I was hospitalized for about five or six days. Then I was discharged. I was sent home to continue my recovery and then I went to the hospital for my bandages to be changed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, if you could find a suitable moment

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: This perhaps is a suitable moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This is what I thought it might be. Mr. Grebic, as I indicated to you already in the beginning, it would only be a short while today that you are examined but the parties will continue your examination tomorrow. We will adjourn until a quarter past 2.00 tomorrow in the afternoon, the same courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
